title: Content-addressed prompt cache + NUMA-aware tokenizer threading
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Reduce prefill-side CPU and memory overhead for multi-tenant workloads by introducing a content-addressed prompt cache (CAPC) combined with NUMA-aware tokenizer threading and lightweight kernel-hint metadata emitted at tokenization time. Goals: (1) avoid repeated tokenization work across identical or semantically-equivalent prompts, (2) minimize cross-NUMA memory traffic and locks during high-concurrency prefill bursts, and (3) attach minimal decode-kernel selection hints so the scheduler can pick faster attention kernels for common patterns.
acceptance_criteria: CAPC returns tokens and KV-prefill artifacts for normalized prompts with <=4ms median latency added to prefill path under 90th percentile load
End-to-end prefill CPU utilization reduced by >=18% for synthetic multi-tenant workload (1000 qps, 50 tenants) compared to baseline
NUMA-aware tokenizer reduces remote memory access cycles by >=25% on internal microbench and does not degrade single-tenant tail latency
Kernel-hint metadata (3-5 bytes) successfully consumed by decode scheduler to prefer reduced-precision / fused-attention kernels for appropriate models in 95% of cache hits
Security review sign-off for hashing algorithm and PII handling completed and documented
Feature flags and metrics instrumentation in Console (per-tenant cache hit rate, eviction rate, CPU savings) available in staging
notes: Conforms with existing prefill cache eviction policy (LRU-ish) but uses content-addressed keys to allow cross-tenant sharing where allowed by opt-in policy
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aditi Rao: Created ticket after spike revealed repeated tokenization for normalized prompts (email signatures, product boilerplate) accounts for ~12% of prefill CPU cycles during steady traffic.

2025-02-18 - Marco Herrera: Spike implemented content-addressed key = SHA256(normalized_prompt) + prompt-schema-version. Prototype caches token list + short KV-prefill blob (serialized with delta compression). Initial microbench shows 22% CPU reduction for 200 qps per-node workload.

2025-02-21 - Design review notes (Sofia Kim): Approve approach but require explicit tenant opt-in for cross-tenant cache hits. Also prefer BLAKE3 over SHA256 for lower CPU and streaming-friendly API. Marked security_review_required.

2025-02-24 - Security (Jon Park): PII risk: hashing normalized prompts may still leak small patterns; recommend canonicalization and salt per-tenant when opt-out=false. Added Confluence checklist for data-flow proof.

2025-02-27 - Eng feedback (Priya Nair): NUMA-threading strategy: pin tokenizer worker pools per-NUMA node and use per-node MPSC queues to avoid locks. Trade-off: increased memory footprint due to per-node cache shards; measured ~6% memory increase acceptable.

2025-02-28 - Marco Herrera: Added kernel-hint output to tokenizer: enum {dense-short, sparse-long, repeating-mask} based on token distribution heuristics. Scheduler accepts hint via request metadata and picks fused attention when supported.

2025-03-01 - QA (Luca Moretti): Integration tests failing intermittently on ephemeral staging due to eviction race; toggled feature-flagged rollout to 5% of traffic until fix. Opening follow-up sub-issue to harden eviction atomics (ENG-55901).
follow_up_actions: ENG-55901: Fix eviction race and add linearizability tests (high priority)
Add per-tenant opt-in UI in Console (PM + UX work) and instrumentation to show cross-tenant sharing (product decision)
Schedule security review and sign-off (expected by 2025-03-10)
